title: Stacking-tuned superconductivity and competing charge-density-wave states in NbSe$_2$
authors: Sandra Sajan, Xinze Yang, Haojie Guo, Tarushi Agarwal, Samuel Mañas-Valero, Carla Boix-Constant, Eugenio Coronado, Fernando de Juan, Eduardo H. da Silva Neto, Ravi P. Singh, Maria N. Gastiasoro, Miguel M. Ugeda
abstract: Layer stacking provides a powerful yet underexplored route for reshaping collective quantum order in van der Waals materials. Here we use high-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to show that the stacking sequence alone can qualitatively transform the charge density and superconducting orders in NbSe$_2$, while preserving the same in-plane atomic structure. Comparing the 4Ha and 2H polytypes, we find that, unlike the ubiquitous triangular incommensurate $3Q^\mathrm{I}$ order of 2H-NbSe$_2$, 4Ha-NbSe$_2$ hosts two competing CDW states with no measurable correlation with local strain: a unidirectional commensurate $1Q^\mathrm{C}$ phase and a triangular incommensurate $3Q^\mathrm{I}$ phase, with $Q^\mathrm{I}=Q^\mathrm{C}+δ$. We introduce a phase-resolved analysis that directly maps the gradient of the CDW phases and reveals vortices bound to the $1Q^\mathrm{C}$ - $3Q^\mathrm{I}$ phase boundaries. These vortices accommodate the momentum mismatch $δ$ through abrupt $2π$ phase slips, providing a mechanism by which distinct charge orders coexist. Superconductivity is also reshaped by stacking, while both polytypes exhibit multiband pairing.
summary: This work demonstrates that the structural polytype of $	ext{NbSe}_2$ dictates its competing electronic orders, particularly CDW and superconductivity. Using STM/STS and Ginzburg-Landau theory, the authors show that $4	ext{Ha}$-$	ext{NbSe}_2$ uniquely hosts coexisting commensurate and incommensurate CDW states stabilized by phase slips. This highlights stacking sequence as a key knob for controlling quantum electronic phases.
main_problem: The study investigates how changing the layer stacking sequence (polytype) of van der Waals materials like NbSe2 can fundamentally alter competing electronic orders, specifically charge-density waves (CDW) and superconductivity.
main_result: The $4	ext{Ha}$ polytype exhibits an intrinsic coexistence of distinct CDW states ($1Q^\mathrm{C}$ and $3Q^\mathrm{I}$) that is not correlated with local strain, a phenomenon explained by phase slips at domain boundaries. Furthermore, the superconducting gap is selectively suppressed in this polytype compared to its $2	ext{H}$ counterpart.
method: The research combines high-resolution Scanning Tunneling Microscopy/Spectroscopy (STM/STS) measurements with theoretical modeling using Ginzburg-Landau formalisms to analyze phase transitions and order parameter dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{NbSe}_2$ in its $4	ext{Ha}$ and $2	ext{H}$ polytypes. The analysis uses a free energy functional derived from Ginzburg-Landau theory to model the complex CDW order parameter, alongside anisotropic two-band McMillan models for superconductivity.

paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the electronic orders of $4	ext{Ha}$ vs $2	ext{H}$ polytypes. It first uses STM/STS to map CDW states, then applies GL theory to model the coexistence mechanism involving phase slips, and finally analyzes superconducting gaps under magnetic fields.
why_interesting: The ability to tune collective quantum order (CDW/SC) simply by changing crystal stacking is a powerful concept for engineering novel electronic phases in 2D materials, relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
